cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A distributed system is a set of independent machines that communicate over a network and coordinate so that, to users, they behave like one system. We build them to scale beyond one machine, stay available when a machine fails, and be closer to users.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Key traits are resource sharing, scalability, fault tolerance and concurrency. The cost is that the network is unreliable: messages can be delayed or lost and nodes fail independently, so you need replication, consensus and careful handling of consistency and partitions.

questions.q: If one node fails, does the system keep working automatically?
questions.a: Not automatically. Fault tolerance must be designed in with replication, health checks and failover.
To scale beyond one machine, stay available through failures, and be closer to users.
The network is unreliable and nodes fail independently.
